name: Natural Material Stress Reduction via Multi-Modal Sensory Convergence
short_description: Natural materials (especially wood) produce stress reduction through convergence of visual-fractal, haptic-thermal, acoustic, olfactory, and ecological channels
structural_pattern: Natural materials — particularly wood, but also natural stone, earth, and plant fibers — produce stress-reduction effects that exceed any single sensory channel's contribution. The effect arises from CONVERGENCE: (1) Visual: natural grain patterns exhibit 1/f spectral profiles (T1); (2) Haptic-thermal: low thermal effusivity maintains skin-temperature contact (MAT1); (3) Acoustic: moderate absorption produces warm acoustics (AX1); (4) Olfactory: VOCs (terpenes) activate olfactory-limbic pathways reducing sympathetic activity; (5) Ecological: natural signatures match statistical regularities the brain is calibrated to. Each channel contributes modest stress reduction; the convergent total is larger than any single channel, and potentially super-additive.
higher_order_principle: Material-domain instantiation of the multi-channel convergence principle (like L3 for daylight). As daylight engages multiple channels simultaneously, natural materials engage visual-fractal, haptic-thermal, acoustic, olfactory, and ecological channels simultaneously. Multi-channel confirmation produces qualitatively greater processing fluency.

convergent_channels.name: visual_fractal
convergent_channels.mechanism: 1/f grain patterns near D≈1.3 → processing fluency

convergent_channels.name: haptic_thermal
convergent_channels.mechanism: Low effusivity → skin-temp maintenance → CT activation

convergent_channels.name: acoustic
convergent_channels.mechanism: Moderate absorption → warm, intimate room acoustics

convergent_channels.name: ecological
convergent_channels.mechanism: Natural signatures match brain's ecological heuristics

wood_optimal_ratio: ~45% wood surface ratio (Tsunetsugu et al., 2007) — inverted-U function

causal_links.evidence_base: T1 mechanism: 1/f spectral profile of natural grain → fractal fluency → positive affect. (Spehar et al., 2003; Taylor et al., 2011)
MAT1 pathway: wood e~400 → skin-temperature maintenance → CT activation → insular comfort signal.
AX1/AX4: wood has moderate absorption (α ~0.1–0.3), producing warm acoustics.
Miyazaki's phytoncide pathway: wood terpenes → olfactory → limbic → reduced sympathetic activity. Li et al. (2006, 2009).
Convergence hypothesis: simultaneous confirmation across channels produces greater stress reduction than sum of individual channels. Material analog of L3 daylight convergence.

scope_conditions: Applies to environments with substantial natural material surfaces — proportion matters (peak at ~45%)
VOC pathway requires UNTREATED or lightly treated natural material
Convergence applies to genuine natural materials, not simulated — laminate engages visual only and may produce MAT3 PE
Cultural moderation: effect demonstrated primarily in Japanese and Scandinavian populations
moderators: Material proportion: inverted-U — too little → insufficient signal; too much → visual monotony
Surface treatment: sealants block VOCs and change thermal properties
Wood species: terpene profiles differ (hinoki, cedar, pine)
Exposure duration: visual/haptic effects rapid; olfactory-autonomic effects build over hours
Building age: new wood releases more VOCs; aged wood develops richer visual/haptic complexity

interactions.nature: T1 is the visual channel of MAT4. Natural grain patterns engage T1.
MAT1 is the haptic-thermal channel of MAT4.
AX1 is the acoustic channel of MAT4.
MAT4 and L3 are structural analogs: multi-channel convergence. L3 = daylight; MAT4 = natural materials.
MAT3 describes cross-modal prediction machinery. MAT4 describes what happens when natural materials PASS all MAT3 checks — full convergence produces 'realness' signal.
